targets.authors: Barsbai, T., Rapoport, H., Steinmayr, A., & Trebesch, C.
targets.title: The effect of labor migration on the diffusion of democracy: evidence from a former Soviet Republic.
targets.evidence_quote: Data-analytic replication attempt to evaluate 9 claims from Barsbai_AmEcoJourn_2017_9OK1
targets.outcome_quote: Result: Prevalence of emigration to the West coefficient is -0.467632 but not statistically significant at p = 0.1904506. This claim was not replicated.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Seven claim verdicts are non-replications, while the flawed-Western-democracy and age-heterogeneity claims are explicitly replicated. Mixed across nine claims from one original paper. These use 2014 election results against the original 2009 findings, hence a different sample, not reproduction.
targets.additional_outcome_quote: Results: Within the population who grew up in the Soviet Union the coefficient of westward migration on Communist votes is -0.3483494 and larger in older group (-0.4511474) than in the younger group (-0.3483494). This claim was replicated.

reasoning: Assigned OSF GUID resolves to the complete SCORE report; project contributors match supplied authors. Report tests nine claims from one original paper using later election data.
